This page is the short, interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each
section has a **Lab task** for the lab computer and one set of questions.

## Key terms

{{< glossary digital-skills digital-literacy digital-competence digcomp competence-area proficiency-level labour-market lifelong-learning >}}

## 1.1 Skills, literacy and competence

- **Digital skills:** what you can do with a device (send an e-mail, fill in a form).
- **Digital literacy:** skills + understanding (you check if information is true).
- **Digital competence:** literacy + good behaviour (you use the tools safely).
- Three levels: **basic** (common apps), **intermediate** (apps at work),
  **advanced** (builds and runs technology).
- Example: Ahmad types fast, but he gives his password to friends. He has
  skills, but not competence.

![Skills, literacy and competence.](images/skills-circles.png){width=66%}

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Your digital week"}
Write five things you did on a computer or a phone this week. Next to each
one, write its level: basic, intermediate or advanced.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Which word, which level?"}
Choose the right answer. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="digital literacy"}
Ahmad types fast, but he gives his password to friends. What does he have?
:   skills, but not competence

Which level is sending an e-mail?
:   basic

Which level is making a chart in a spreadsheet at work?
:   intermediate

Which level is writing programs?
:   advanced

Which word means using digital tools safely and responsibly?
:   digital competence
:::
:::

## 1.2 DigComp: five areas of digital skills

- **DigComp** is a European list of the digital skills that every person needs.
- Five areas: 1 information and data, 2 communication and collaboration,
  3 content creation, 4 safety, 5 problem solving.
- Levels in four groups: **foundation** (with help), **intermediate** (alone),
  **advanced** (helps others), **highly specialised** (leads others).
- Programming is only one small part of DigComp.

![The five DigComp areas.](images/digcomp-areas.png){width=96%}

{{< sim file="sims/digcomp-check.html" poster="sims/digcomp-check.png" title="DigComp self-check" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Your DigComp profile"}
Do the **DigComp self-check** above. Your answers stay in this browser only.
Find your strongest and your weakest area. Save your profile as a PDF for the
next lab session.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Which DigComp area?"}
Choose the DigComp area.

::: {.match extra="programming"}
You check if a message about free phones is true.
:   information and data

You send your homework to your teacher with a polite note.
:   communication and collaboration

You make a birthday card with a photo.
:   digital content creation

You use a screen lock on your phone.
:   safety

You cannot make a chart yet, so you watch a short online lesson.
:   problem solving
:::
:::

## 1.3 Why every job needs digital skills

- **Labour market:** people look for work, employers look for workers.
- Almost every job is digital: shops, banks, schools and offices.
- Computers do the simple, repeated tasks. People use and check the programs.
- Apps change often, so workers keep learning: **lifelong learning**.

![Every job uses digital tools.](images/jobs.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · A real job advert"}
Find one real job advert in your field of study. Copy three requirements into
a document. Write the DigComp area of each one. Save it as `job-advert.docx`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Skills at work"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="fewer digital skills|one app for life"}
Computers do the simple, repeated tasks. What must people do now?
:   use and check the programs

What do we call learning new skills during your whole working life?
:   lifelong learning

What do we call the place where people look for work?
:   the labour market

A job advert asks for "a visitor list in a spreadsheet". Which area?
:   information and data

A job advert asks to "keep customer data private". Which area?
:   safety
:::
:::

## Game challenge: hiring at Sunrise Company {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Sunrise Company** has an office and a shop. It needs an office assistant
and a sales assistant. The office assistant answers the e-mails of customers.
The sales assistant makes short videos about new products. Every worker
signs in with a code on the phone.

Play the hiring desk: put each task in its DigComp area, read the levels of
the people, and choose the right person.

{{< sim file="sims/hiring-desk.html" poster="sims/hiring-desk.png" title="Hiring Desk: sort the skills, hire the team" kind="game" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Read the people (harder)"}
Sunrise Company: the office assistant answers e-mails from customers; the
sales assistant makes short videos; every worker signs in with a code on the
phone. Choose the DigComp area or the group of levels.

::: {.match extra="problem solving|highly specialised"}
Answering e-mails from customers.
:   communication and collaboration

Making short videos about new products.
:   digital content creation

Signing in with a code on the phone.
:   safety

A person who can send a file only with help.
:   foundation

A person who teaches other workers a new app.
:   advanced
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Skills, literacy, competence: each one is bigger than the one before.
- Three levels: basic, intermediate, advanced.
- DigComp has five areas and four groups of levels.
- Programming is only one small part of digital skills.
- Every job is digital, so workers keep learning.
